title: Offline-first, EAR99-by-design structured orders, tasks, reports and LOGSTAT object layer with CRDT merge for TAK-CIV, sold first to public-safety incident command, National Guard and allied light units, with the merge model licensable to HQ planning and C2 platform owners
problem: Incident commanders, National Guard battalion staffs and allied light units that already run TAK on unclassified networks still move orders, assignments, status reports and sustainment/resource status as paper ICS forms, chat, voice and spreadsheets that do not merge cleanly when nodes reconnect after working disconnected, so the picture diverges between the command post, field elements and higher headquarters.

user.exact_role: Incident commander / planning section chief / resource unit leader on an all-hazards or wildland incident management team; National Guard battalion S3/S4 and battle captain on state active duty or Title 32 domestic missions; allied light-infantry company/battalion staff on ATAK
organization_examples: State wildland fire agencies and interagency IMTs using WFTAK (Colorado CoE, FAM IM Tools)
Municipal fire departments using TAK with FirstNet (e.g., Green Bay Metro Fire, 2025)
Army/Air National Guard elements on domestic response (147th ASOS Hurricane Harvey use of ATAK; 2025 wildfire response)
Bundeswehr light units via Cyber Innovation Hub pilots; NATO DIANA 2027 'operational resilience' challenge cohort

current_workflow: Incident: IC fills ICS 201 briefing and ICS 202/204/209 on paper or Word/PDF templates; assignments are read out at briefings; resources tracked on T-cards/whiteboards or an IMS web app that needs connectivity; TAK shows PLI and markers only
Field elements report status by radio/phone/chat; planning section re-keys into forms each operational period; disconnected divisions bring paper back to the ICP

Guard battalion: receives WARNORD/OPORD as PDF/PowerPoint over intermittent links; tracks tasks, SITREP/LOGSTAT/PERSTAT on spreadsheets and chat; ATAK data packages carry graphics; on reconnect, reports are re-typed into higher's format
Allied light unit: SitaWare Edge/Frontline where fielded, otherwise ATAK plus voice; orders as documents
After each displacement/reconnect, staff manually reconcile which version of the assignment or report is current
current_solution: Paper NIMS ICS forms (FEMA ICS forms booklet); TAK Server 'Data Sync' missions (government, free) that re-sync map items, files, logs and chat missed while disconnected but carry no structured order/report/LOGSTAT objects and no CRDT merge; commercial incident-management software (Tablet Command, Resgrid IC with offline-first ICS-201 timeline, Intterra, Juvare WebEOC, Veoci and the 10+ products in the DHS SAVER 2022 market survey); Ditto's Edge Sync plugin for ATAK (company claim) for peer-to-peer CRDT sync of ATAK objects; on the military side Onebrief (offline tactical access 'underway', company statement), SBMC clients (Anduril/Rivet, ATAK-backward-compatible), Systematic SitaWare Edge tasking; Meshtastic/goTenna mesh transports for TAK.
failure: Structured content has no object model in TAK: it travels as files, chat and data packages, so two nodes that edited the same assignment or report while partitioned cannot merge and someone re-keys by hand; commercial IMS tools are cloud-first (Resgrid excepted, queue-and-replay not multi-writer merge) and not TAK-native; ~80% of wildland responders carry iOS devices where iTAK accepts no third-party plugins, so an ATAK-CIV plugin alone cannot reach them; the Guard has no program office or budget line for a battalion orders/reports app and the allied path is small pilots.

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Three structural reasons, none of which a new entrant changes. (1) The layer is split across owners who each solve their own slice: the TAK Product Center ships free Data Sync missions for map items/files/chat; Ditto sells the CRDT sync engine for ATAK; public-safety IMS vendors (Tablet Command, Resgrid, Intterra, WebEOC, Veoci) own the ICS forms workflow in web/iOS apps; Onebrief/Anduril/Rivet/Systematic own the military orders layer. Nobody has combined 'structured order/report objects + multi-writer merge + TAK-native' because each owner's customers are satisfied enough by their slice. (2) The public-safety buyer base is thousands of agencies with GPC/grant-sized software budgets, iOS-majority devices (iTAK has no plugin architecture), and adoption barriers that are training and community rather than features (TAK Public Safety 501(c)(3) exists for exactly this). (3) The 'license the merge model' thesis fails on commoditization: CRDT engines are open source (Automerge, Yjs) or already sold (Ditto), and the domain schemas (NIMS ICS forms, FM 6-0/FM 4-0 report formats) are public standards, so the only proprietary asset would be integration work, which is services.
technical_wedge: A TAK-Server-side 'structured objects' service (extending the documented mission/Data Sync API) plus an ATAK-CIV plugin and an iOS/web companion app, that represents ICS 201/204/209/214 (public safety) and WARNORD/FRAGO tasks, SITREP/LOGSTAT/PERSTAT (Guard/allied) as versioned JSON objects with a CRDT merge model tuned to forms (per-field last-writer-wins with causal history, list merges for assignments/resources, explicit conflict surfacing for quantities), transported as compact CoT/mission deltas over Meshtastic/goTenna/FirstNet, so that field elements that edit while disconnected reconcile automatically on reconnect without re-keying.

mvp.what: Open-source TAK Server extension + ATAK-CIV plugin + iOS/web companion implementing ICS 204/209/214 and a LOGSTAT/SITREP object with CRDT merge, running on commercial Android/iOS devices and Meshtastic radios
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes: five EUDs plus a laptop ICP/TOC with deliberate partitions and a command-post jump; measure convergence time, bytes per object, zero manual re-keying; demo at a state wildland exercise or a Guard battalion drill weekend (no program office needed)
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That multi-writer edits to assignments, resource status and LOGSTAT quantities made during a 6-hour partition merge with no duplicates or lost updates, on iOS as well as Android, and that a planning section produces the next operational period's ICS 204s faster than with paper/Word; and that at least one agency will pay for it rather than use free TAK Data Sync plus its existing IMS

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes. TPC can add structured form objects to Data Sync missions; Ditto can ship a schema pack on its existing ATAK plugin; Tablet Command/Intterra can add offline multi-writer merge; Onebrief/Anduril already cover the military layer; Motorola/Genasys-class public-safety incumbents could buy any of them. Each could do so within one product cycle; none has a reason to license a merge model they can take from open source.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Reject as a venture. The only durable asset would be a large installed base of agencies using an open standard the startup steers (a community/standards play, e.g., a de facto ICS-object schema for TAK), which is a slow, low-margin path better suited to a nonprofit or an open-source-plus-services company. It can win as a small, bootstrapped niche product or as an acquihire by Ditto, TPC contractors (PAR Government), Onebrief or an IMS vendor; that is a feature/acquihire path, not venture scale.

regulatory_burden.explanation: A civil incident-management product on open-source ATAK-CIV/TAK Server with public ICS schemas is ordinarily commercial software (EAR99 is plausible but must be confirmed by counsel); no ATO, CUI or clearance is needed for public-safety pilots, though agencies may require CJIS-adjacent and state security reviews and StateRAMP for hosted services. The burden rises to medium for Guard use (Army network ATO, CMMC if CUI flows, TAK-GOV gating) and for allied pilots (possible ITAR defense-service exposure when integrating for a foreign military).
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: On the public-safety, EAR99/open-source path the Indonesian founder is largely unconstrained (E07-F17); SBIR/STTR (DHS or Army) would require a >50% U.S.-person-owned cap table (13 CFR 121.702); any Guard/military variant with controlled technical data or a foreign-military integration would need counsel on deemed exports and defense services; no legal judgment made.

dual_use_potential.explanation: The product is dual-use by construction: NIMS ICS forms for public safety and doctrinal orders/reports for Guard/allied units share the same object-and-merge core; TAK itself is used by both communities. The catch is that dual-use here means two small, fragmented markets rather than one large commercial one.

defensibility.explanation: Weak. CRDT merge is commoditized (Automerge/Yjs/Ditto); schemas are public standards; TAK is government-owned and free; switching cost for an agency is low. Only an installed base across many agencies and IMTs, plus becoming the de facto TAK ICS-object schema, would create modest lock-in - and that is a community/standards outcome, not a proprietary one.

why_now: Public-safety TAK adoption has crossed from pilots to routine use (DHS S&T iTAK release, WFTAK interagency server, TAK Public Safety nonprofit founded 2024, FirstNet-paired municipal use 2025); cheap LoRa mesh (Meshtastic ATAK forwarder; Feb 2026 iOS built-in TAK server) makes disconnected multi-node operation common outside the military; CRDT libraries are production-grade; and the Army's own 2025-2026 DDIL focus (Ivy Sting 4, SBMC ATAK compatibility) has normalized the idea of structured content over tactical links. Against this, the same period saw Ditto, Resgrid and TPC Data Sync ship the adjacent pieces, so the window is for a niche product, not a category.
killer_risk: The venture thesis rests on licensing a merge model that is already commoditized (open-source CRDTs; Ditto's funded ATAK sync plugin) into markets that are either fragmented and grant-sized (thousands of public-safety agencies, iOS-majority devices that reject plugins, adoption gated by training) or unfunded at this layer (Guard has no program office or line; allied entry is EUR 100k DIANA grants and CIHBw pilots) - so even success is a small SaaS/open-source-plus-services business or an acquihire, not a venture-scale company, and TPC or an IMS vendor can add structured offline forms in one release.
